svg.text: Audit finding 9, part 1-2: quantitative TCE/DAVE/TPM benchmark + a real multi-sector blind test
Closing two of the three gaps that stand between a reproducible harness and genuine scientific meaning. Numbers read from our own measured reports.
Measure-only: no gate moved, no bundle hash or money path touched, discoveryClaim false.
P79 BENCHMARK
We track the BLS/TCE limit
Re-implemented TCE BLS SNR + >=3-transit / SNR>=7 rule,
DAVE blend FPP, and a TPM logistic fit to OUR p47 grid.
Cells the TCE rule ACCEPTS: 74% measured completeness.
Cells it REJECTS: 0% (24 accept / 6 reject cells).
=> our detector's completeness follows the standard BLS/TCE
detection limit on real photometry (8 offline tests).
P78 BLIND TEST
Real per-sector, scaled
24 real SPOC hosts (all >=2 sectors): 10 injected,
14 null, 55 period-clusters. Not stand-in, not stitched.
2-sector bar: accepted recall 0.80 (8/10).
Corroboration histogram (1..5 sectors): 38/13/1/3/0.
Raw precision 16% -> under the 2-sector bar 47%.
P49 could not show this: it stitched sectors and forced 1.
HONEST VERDICT
Corroboration helps, is not enough
False-accepts under the 2-sector bar: 9.
Requiring 2 independent sectors only roughly TRIPLES precision
(16% -> 47%) and does NOT zero it out.
Coherent systematics / aliases RECUR across sectors, so period-
only corroboration is necessary but NOT sufficient for a claim.
Blending is not the binding constraint (DAVE FPP for a faint
neighbour ~ 0.3%) -- systematics are.
GAP 3 (IN PROGRESS)
Independent validation
The 0/2 external-candidate result was structural: the critic
audits with an empty catalog, so an outside claim caps at
needs-more-data by design -- it can never self-validate.
P80 (next): detect BLIND (no ephemeris fed) on real hosts, then
cross-match a corroborated detection against an INDEPENDENT
published catalog -- confirmation from a source we did NOT
use to detect, breaking the circularity.
SpaceDataRig/space-data-rig - spacedatarig.app - all numbers re-derivable via npm run p78:blind-multisector / p79:benchmark.
